description: Team Stellarian s a dedicated solo-driven tech and innovation initiative passionate about bridging the gap between complex space science and immersive digital storytelling. Driven by a deep curiosity for the cosmos and modern web architecture, CodeEx specializes in transforming raw archival data into interactive, high-impact web experiences that educate and inspire the next generation of space explorers."Silent Sentinels: Echoes of Space Exploration"—a web museum.
summary: Silent Sentinels is an immersive digital web museum that showcases historical hardware left behind by NASA across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. How it works: Users navigate through a cinematic, high-graphics interface to explore interactive artifact cards representing legendary rovers and landers (like Apollo descent stages and Viking landers). The app connects dynamically in real-time to official NASA public services—fetching archival photographs and captions from the NASA Image and Video Library API ([https://images-api.nasa.gov](https://images-api.nasa.gov)) and mission investigation data from the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS). It features first-person narrative logs from the spacecrafts' perspectives, an interactive educational "Talk to the Sentinel" dialogue panel, and a gamified "Space Cadet" mini-quiz.
details: Silent Sentinels: Echoes of Space Exploration ([https://lunar-relic.lovable.app/#top](https://lunar-relic.lovable.app/#top)) is an interactive, cinematic web museum built using Lovable.dev, modern responsive CSS/Tailwind glassmorphism UI, and real-time integrations with the official NASA Image and Video Library API ([https://images-api.nasa.gov](https://images-api.nasa.gov)) and NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) investigation records. Designed specifically for school-age space enthusiasts to align with the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, the platform transforms static historical records into a living digital experience where discarded NASA hardware across the Moon, Mars, and deep space tells its own story through first-person narrative journals, an interactive "Talk to the Sentinel" dialogue channel, and a gamified Space Cadet mini-quiz. By prioritizing accessibility, visual engagement, and real scientific API authenticity, the project bridges modern web engineering with space storytelling to make planetary history inspiring, memorable, and universally accessible to the next generation of STEM explorers.
